notes: Hand-entered reward rules, checked against issuer pages on the as_of date. Rates are per $1 (3 = 3x points or 3% cash back). Spend above a cap earns rate_after. Each card names a points_program; the value of one point in cents lives in point_programs and can be overridden per call or per server (see README). Every category rule has valid_from and valid_until (ISO dates, inclusive; null means no known start or end). A category-wide promotion is modeled in the card's promotions list only when the issuer's own page shows its terms and end date, and it records its own source_url and as_of. Bonuses that depend on booking channel or merchant lists, and promotions without a published end date, are listed under not_modeled instead of being approximated.

cash.name: Cash back
cash.basis: Cash back is worth face value.

chase_ultimate_rewards.name: Chase Ultimate Rewards
chase_ultimate_rewards.basis: Cash-back value: Chase says 100 points = $1 cash back (Freedom Unlimited terms). Pay with Points at Amazon/PayPal is 0.8 cents. Transfers to airline and hotel partners can be worth more, but only if you also hold a Sapphire or Ink card that can transfer.

amex_membership_rewards.name: American Express Membership Rewards
amex_membership_rewards.basis: Amex doesn't publish a cents-per-point value. 1 cent is a neutral baseline: statement credits are generally worth less, and transfers to Amex's airline and hotel partners can be worth more. Many people value these points at 1.5 to 2 cents.

citi_thankyou.name: Citi ThankYou
citi_thankyou.basis: Citi says 10,000 points = $100 statement credit, direct deposit or check (Double Cash page). Higher values need a premium Citi card that can transfer.
